# Shared-rim section regression archive

`shared-rims.3dm` contains two generated MIT-suite Breps, extracted without changing their geometry:

- `S-split-rim-local`: definition f278ad58-75b4-5a0c-8905-f59c849f9426, object 3995308d-bd8e-5fb9-aa9f-3852b1ca2a82, in definition-local coordinates. Source: `curved-repeat/curved-perf-S-blocks.3dm`, SHA-256 `4D48286CB5634BFA8A6B5BF9AF1F680EC678B3D4B6BF925F2FAB96990A977A10`.
- `M-partial-rim-world`: instance 22565916-08dc-5f70-8b60-f5538d8a52c9 of definition ecaa0f35-5255-58e4-bead-48ed18d1ca8e, with the recorded instance transform applied once. Source: `models/curved-perf-M-blocks.3dm`, SHA-256 `B0C49C4F5982335D990C8A4DAD5EC022AB91B0CF650DF26BEC2B243AA4A4DE26`.

Both source archives were generated by `tools/models/curved.py` and read from the read-only evidence worktree `t3-d6bdd8e8-f1e6b3c68a0e104e/artifacts/`. Only object names/IDs are new in this minimal archive. The regression tests require valid solid topology and shared-edge coverage; they do not infer solid validity from Rhino's `IsSolid` flag alone. The split-rim cylinder and genuinely self-intersecting sweep are constructed directly in `CurvedSectionRegressionTests` to keep their independent geometry/oracles reviewable.

Frozen archive SHA-256: 8E69EC5F1561AF8115EDC951AB6F4A4750A828F54A98553769C9F58D9E22B737 (39,639 bytes). Tests use the original metre-valued coordinates and explicit modelling tolerance; archive unit metadata does not rescale the geometry.
